newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Investors warned about unlicensed commodity shops.
newsitem.headline: Investors warned about unlicensed commodity shops.

text.p: The Singapore Commodity Exchange (SICOM) has asked potential investors to trade through the exchange's nine broker members and be wary of unlicensed trading houses, the Sunday Times newspaper said.

It said rubber and coffee were the only commodities regulated under Singapore's Commodity Futures Act and Regulations, but a number of unlicensed outlets were also dealing in ungazetted commodities such as cotton, pork belly and soybeans.
These unlicensed houses tended to entice people with little financial knowledge into investing in commodity futures and then siphon off their funds, the paper said.

Quoting unnamed industry sources, it said there were about seven such shops in the market and they had moved back into commodities trading from foreign exchange after the Futures Trading Act, which covers forex, was amended last year.
It said SICOM member brokers were regulated by the exchange and the Trade Development Board.
They are required to keep clients' accounts separate from the firm's business and have a minimum of Singapore $1 million in cash deposited with the exchange and S$1 million in net assets.
